text:
Sara V: FYI -- after the driver rollout to 535.86 in us-west2 we're seeing a spike of H100/Hopper kernel verification failures and NCCL stalls. Affects both hosted and dedicated H100 SKUs. Rolling nodes back to 530 helped some but not all nodes.

Sara V: paste of representative logs: 
```
[ERROR] kernel_verify: ptx_version_mismatch sm=90 comp=ptx v=14 required>=15 
[WARN] ptx_jit_fallback: runtime_jit_enabled=1 image=...sm90...
[nccl] Allgather timed out: rank 3 -> rank 0 (timeout 120s)
```

Ajay P: saw the same in our canary pool at 02:12. Autoscaler marked several H100 nodes Unready and created replacements, which then also failed healthchecks. Looks like PTX version mismatch triggers nvrtc/cubin rejection during kernel load.

Leah M: Impact estimate from infra dashboard: ~52 H100 nodes flapping in us-west2, ~30% effective H100 capacity drop for the region. Dedicated customers hit higher error rates. We're also burning money from double-provisioning while autoscaler tries to heal.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: driver-upgrade/us-west2 -> 535.86 @ 2026-03-16T02:15:00Z :white_check_mark:

Ryan C: quick checks to run if you haven't: 
- `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` 
- `cuobjdump --dump-ptx /path/to/cubin | head -n 5` to inspect PTX version embedded in kernels 
- `dmesg | grep -i ptx` / `journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service`

Kyle H: short-term mitigation options: 
1) Pin nodepool for Hopper SKUs back to 530 (rollback) 
2) Taint Hopper nodes and move critical loads to Ampere for now 
3) Patch runtime to avoid JITing PTX when possible (force precompiled cubins) 
4) Add a canary gate to stop driver rollout to remaining regions

Ajay P: tried env hack `CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1` on one node — reduced kernel-verify spam but several models still fail at load because driver refuses older cubins. Not a complete fix.

Leah M: Does this smell like a PTX ABI bump from our compiler chain? We recently landed a minor change in the compile tool that emits ptx v15 for some kernels. If driver 535 expects different compatibility, we need to coordinate with eng-runtime.

Ryan C: yep, likely PTX->SASS compatibility shift. Driver minimums can reject older cubins if JIT can't reconcile. Also NCCL stack version mismatch can surface as timeouts when collective kernels fail to load. Check installed libcudart/cuda-toolkit on node images.

Sara V: Immediate ask: can infra pause the driver rollout to eu/us-other regions? And create a pinned 530 nodepool for us-west2 so we stop draining running instances.

Kyle H: I'll open the nodepool pinning and rollback PR now and add a cluster-level rollout-hold. If folks confirm, I'll flip autoscaler behavior to avoid creating new Hopper nodes until we resolve.

ops-bot: incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-16-001 (investigating) -- triage channel #incidents-2026-03-16

Leah M: Also flagging product: we should notify customers on Dedicated whose capacity is impacted. Ops -> CS handoff needed.

Ajay P: long-term: we need a compatibility matrix that ties compiler PTX targets, driver minimums, and runtime kernel loaders. And an automated canary that runs a small allreduce across a fresh driver image before rolling.

Ryan C: Agreed. For next steps I'm going to: (1) gather `cuobjdump` outputs from a failed cubin, (2) check toolchain that produced the cubin, (3) run a small repro on a standalone Hopper node to reproduce load-time failure and NCCL hang.

Sara V: Great — keep updates here. If anyone finds an immediate rollback success rate metric, paste it. Otherwise we'll track in INCIDENT-2026-03-16-001. :triage:
